branches.title: When does video 3D consistency predict downstream failure?
branches.stage: literature conflict: metric novelty blocked; pivot under audit
branches.question: Do geometry-specific failures in generated video predict downstream task errors after matching perceptual quality and camera motion?
branches.novelty: MEt3R (CVPR 2025) compares multi-view consistency; PDI-Bench (2026) already measures object rigidity and motion in generated video; PAIWorld (2026) studies robotic multi-view geometry. A generic rigidity metric alone is NOT a new contribution. Seek a causal downstream link or a falsifiable limitation of existing scores.
branches.pilot: Use an existing geometry-labeled benchmark or render 20 rigid scenes. Apply controlled object deformation at fixed camera trajectory and quality, then test whether PDI/MEt3R scores and a simple planner change in a monotone way. No video generator training.
branches.stop: Stop if the effect is already established by prior downstream planning studies, or if planner failure cannot be attributed to geometry rather than realism.

branches.title: Mask selection as a side channel
branches.stage: formal metric error corrected; position-channel pilot designed; zero experimental runs
branches.question: Can a content-dependent adaptive sampler encode hidden-image information through selected patch positions, and does this bias masked-image learning?
branches.novelty: CORRECTION: the earlier I(Y; M | V) proposal is identically zero when V includes spatial positions of visible patches, since M is the complement of those positions. This is a definitional problem, NOT negative empirical evidence. Informative missingness (GRU-D), adaptive token selection (AdaMAE) and adaptive masking are established. The only plausible new claim concerns mask-policy-induced shortcut learning under carefully controlled sample selection; no novelty claim yet.
branches.pilot: Define S=visible position set, B=values of visible patches without their indices, and T=(S,B) as actual encoder input. Compare position-only S probe, content-only B probe, and S+B probe on a balanced synthetic dataset engineered so visible patch values are identical across labels while the adaptive policy uses unseen context to select blank positions. Compare fixed/random masks and a selector with no access to hidden context; hold count, grid, split and compute fixed. Then test whether a public MAE checkpoint's advantage survives masking-policy swaps and held-out inputs. Report I(Y;S|B) ONLY with B explicitly excluding position indices, not the invalid I(Y;M|T). This sanity example is not evidence of publication novelty. Toy CPU; actual pretrained model small GPU if needed.
branches.stop: If the position-only control does not carry repeatable information on held-out inputs, or the shortcut has no measurable representation/downstream effect after policy controls, retire the performance-inflation claim. Review direct prior art before submitting.

branches.title: Interpretability of layer positions and feature routing
branches.question: Do particular attention heads or layer locations carry causal semantic information beyond easy probe correlations?
branches.novelty: Prior work already finds OCR heads with a verbalization lens; cannot repeat that claim.
branches.pilot: Replicate one released causal intervention on a small vision-language model; compare target-head ablation, layer-matched random heads and input controls.
branches.stop: If effects vanish against layer-matched controls, record a negative result.

branches.title: Entity linking recall under fixed candidate cost
branches.stage: strong 2025-26 budgeted and query-adaptive overlap; all-links global-budget objective proposed; zero runs
branches.question: For source entities with multiple true target links, can calibrated estimates of the maximum true-match retrieval rank allocate a fixed global comparison budget to improve complete-link coverage against strong progressive and query-adaptive baselines?
branches.novelty: Budget scheduling itself is not new: Progressive Entity Resolution (2025) and CIKM 2026 SPER schedule under finite comparisons; QASP (Jul 2026) learns per-query recall curves to tune search effort. BEACON (SIGMOD 2026) has a different annotation-budget objective. Candidate gap, NOT validated novelty: global budget across many source queries with probability of retrieving ALL true links per source, explicit zero-link handling, robust calibration/fairness and matcher time. A textbook multiple-choice knapsack formulation alone is not publishable.
branches.pilot: Define T_i=max rank of all known true targets for positive query i (T_i=infinity if ranking omits a known positive); F_i(k)=Pr(T_i<=k | query features). Choose nonnegative K_i to maximize sum_i F_i(K_i), subject to sum_i K_i<=B, comparing optimal oracle (test upper bound only), uniform K, random allocation, confidence-gap heuristic, QASP-inspired predicted pair-recall curves, progressive-ER scheduler, and calibrated max-rank curve. Lock untouched multi-link test and dev/test split; evaluate complete-link coverage, pair recall, group recall by multiplicity/address/script, matcher and ranking wall time incl prediction overhead, p95/p99 candidate caps. Exclude zero-link queries from positive-query coverage or report separately, since vacuous completion would inflate it. Initial work cached-rank CPU, not a new compute run. Stop if full-link improvement disappears at matched actual CPU time or established method covers the same objective.
branches.stop: Retire novelty if calibrated max-rank scheduling fails to beat QASP-style query-adaptive and progressive-ER schedulers on untouched multi-link queries under the same retrieval+prediction+matcher time and total candidate budget, or closest papers already optimize identical complete-link objective.

branches.title: Budget-matched pretraining data selection
branches.question: Can cheap data selection beat uniform sampling at the same tokens, wall-clock time, and selection overhead?
branches.novelty: Compare to strong recent data-mixture and data-selection baselines, not only uniform.
branches.pilot: Run small-model repeated seeds on fixed corpora, report selection compute plus training compute and held-out perplexity.
branches.stop: If total-cost gains disappear, pivot to an analysis of where selection fails.

branches.title: Do temporal boundaries help downstream memory?
branches.stage: generic event/boundary sampling heavily covered; downstream marginal-utility audit only; no new runs
branches.question: Can detected event boundaries improve temporal retrieval or question answering at equal frame budget?
branches.novelty: Boundary-guided frame sampling predates this work (BMVC 2021), and long-video QA methods already curate query/event-relevant frames at fixed token budgets (Ground, Cover, and Refine 2026; MemoryCard 2026). Claiming first boundary-based QA sampling would be false. Narrower question: whether VIDEO-GENERIC GEBD boundaries, without text/query conditioning, have incremental QA value over equally dense semantic-event and query-aware selectors, and at what noise scale.
branches.pilot: Fixed 16/32-frame budgets, one frozen video QA model. Compare uniform, random, GEBD oracle, predicted GEBD, semantically selected events, and matched query-aware selector. Lock all question annotations and timestamp window, report temporal-relation vs object-identity QA separately plus frame-selection oracle gap and detector cost. First run a small diagnostic on available annotated clips, then require a disjoint larger public set before a paper claim.
branches.stop: Stop generic boundary-as-sampler idea if it offers no gain beyond matched semantic/query-aware selectors on unseen videos or only oracle GT boundaries help.

branches.title: Structured conditions versus captions in action recognition
branches.question: When does verifying discrete temporal conditions outperform a descriptive video caption?
branches.novelty: Simple action benchmarks may make both approaches similar; avoid dataset-specific claims.
branches.pilot: Select temporal minimal-pair actions; fix the video encoder and reasoner, match inference tokens, compare condition-based and caption-based evidence.
branches.stop: If both are tied on hard temporal shifts, refocus on calibration/failure analysis.

branches.title: Agent-made experiments that survive audit
branches.stage: agent evaluation overlap widened; replication failure not assumed; no runs
branches.question: Can a constrained research agent make real improvements under withheld tests and a counted human-intervention budget?
branches.novelty: Autoresearch, CausalVerify, and ICML 2026 DeepAnalyze already cover agentic data research. Bertran/Roth/Wu (2026) finds many agent-found methods generalize despite adaptive search, and deliberate overfitting fails independent reproduction. Tang/Yang (2026) finds AI agents' scientific ideas concentrate near seed literature. The gap must measure WHEN reproducibility and idea diversity break, not assume all agent experiments are invalid or that idea proliferation adds novelty.
branches.pilot: Choose a public constrained agent research task; preregister holdout seeds and data before agent search. Compare short description-only reproduction, code-replay reproduction, and unchanged baseline at equal wall-clock/compute/API-call budget. Include deliberate overfit positive control and quantify topic/idea diversity against citation-based nearest-neighbor baselines. Split any exploratory versus confirmatory tests. No task executed.
branches.stop: If full accounting removes the apparent improvement or a published agent-audit benchmark already tests the same selection-bias protocol, pivot to a reproducibility report rather than a novelty claim.

branches.title: Audio-event segmentation at matched compute
branches.question: Can a simple constrained decoder improve boundaries without a larger speech model?
branches.novelty: Event segmentation already has many decoders; inspect benchmark leakage and timing conventions.

branches.title: Causal study of generated-video geometry errors in robot planning
branches.stage: geometry-to-action question remains speculative; controller margin now an explicit stratification; zero runs
branches.question: For a fixed robot planner and task, which kinds and severity of generated-video geometry faults actually change plan feasibility, rather than only visual similarity?
branches.novelty: What-If World (2026) already benchmarks paired physical interventions in generated driving/manipulation videos, but explicitly leaves downstream utility unmeasured. CausalNav (Aug 2026) reports that structural world-model fidelity need not predict control benefit. ExecutionBridge (Oct 2026) studies a frozen planner under controller-induced execution shift. A general 'causal videos for planning' claim is NOT novel. Candidate: isolate exactly when rigid-object 3D geometry errors flip a frozen planner's action ranking, with matched visual corruption and oracle state controls. Geometric Action Model (2026) explicitly couples geometry to robotic actions, so geometry/action relevance itself is not a novel claim. Retain a narrowly calibrated geometry-fault intervention and matched planner-margin analysis, not a new generic geometry score.
branches.pilot: Start with a reproducible 2D tabletop/grid setup: 2 obstacle configurations × 3 distortion strengths × 3 independent seeds (18 paired scenarios), fixed initial scene, camera, goals, planner, scoring and proposals. Geometric edits must not alter task truth. Compare action-ranking flips, collisions, margin to next-best action, PDI/MEt3R-type score, and appearance-matched non-geometric corruptions. Positive evidence must replicate on withheld scenes before any 3D claims. This is a PROPOSED design; zero runs. Before running, predefine the unperturbed best-vs-second-best planner cost margin delta. Stratify clearance-margin regimes; compare geometry-fault effect to noise with similar image/perceptual change. Report absolute action regret with ground-truth planner costs, not only a flip count. One failure in 18 toy scenarios is illustrative, not publishable; extend to independent 3D scenes if pilot passes.
branches.stop: If 2026 prior work already tests geometry-specific action-ranking regret under frozen policies, or distortion effects disappear after matching appearance and oracle state, retire/pivot. No RSS abstract without a genuinely distinct mechanism and controlled pilot.

branches.title: Small formal proofs for retrieval and selection
branches.stage: elementary exact formulation defined (not novel); identify nontrivial restricted theorem or abandon theory claim
branches.question: Under what realistic constraints on calibration error, fairness or retrieval costs can a complete-link global-budget allocation guarantee robust coverage?
branches.novelty: The standard deterministic all-link allocation problem reduces to choosing per-query ranks under a total budget (multiple-choice knapsack or threshold-cost selection); this alone is a known optimization structure, not an original theorem. Seek a genuine robustness or calibration result, and compare established budgeted ranking/scheduling literature.
branches.pilot: Derive max-rank completion score F_i(k), show by a six-true-link counterexample that pair recall and complete-link coverage select different allocations: A has positives at ranks 1-4; B and C each have their only positive at rank 2; budget 4 gives A:4/B:0/C:0 => 4/6 pairs, 1/3 complete vs A:0/B:2/C:2 => 2/6 pairs, 2/3 complete. This is an analytic example only. Implement exhaustive small-instance verifier only if a runnable environment is available, then check calibration-error stability and counterexamples.
branches.stop: If bound is vacuous under realistic distributions, retire.

branches.title: Transfer of synthetic-image evaluation to biology
branches.stage: new MIDL 2027 deadline; biologically valid topology/lineage controls required; no pilot run
branches.question: Do synthetic microscopy video quality scores predict cell-count, division-lineage, and tracking failures under matched appearance changes?
branches.novelty: 2025 microscopy video diffusion work already evaluates morphology, proliferation and migration in generated cell videos; Cell Tracking Challenge provides established tracking metrics. A generic 'biological geometry consistency' score would overlap existing evaluations. Need test whether visual/video metrics can miss biologically material lineage/topology errors, with licensed public data and explicit nonclinical scope.
branches.pilot: Choose released Cell Tracking Challenge time-lapse sequences with labels. Construct matched editing pairs: one changes only brightness/texture, one inserts a division, disappearance, or impossible identity switch at controlled severity. Blind labels and compare 2-3 published image/video quality scores with cell count, division-timing, lineage and tracking metrics on held-out sequences. First test without training (CPU image edits and existing segmentation/tracking checkpoints). No clinical outcome claims without external validation.
branches.stop: Do not target MIDL main/full clinical track if only toy cells, no image-grounded biologically valid intervention, or effects already captured by existing cell-tracking evaluation; use a reproducibility/method note when appropriate.

branches.title: Are networked research experiments truly reproducible?
branches.question: How often do agent-driven optimization claims vanish under controlled placement, contention and seed variance?
branches.novelty: A benchmark alone needs a novel reproducibility protocol or generalizable systems finding.
branches.pilot: Run small synthetic services with controlled load and resource contention; measure throughput, latency and variance before/after each agent change.
branches.stop: If differences are explainable by noise, don't claim an optimization.
